ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r1.claim: “In the evening” means late day through midnight; Abu al-Layth narrows it to after the afternoon prayer.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r1.anchor: {وجآءوا أباهم عشآء} ظرف أي في آخر النهار فإن العشاء آخر النهار إلى نصف الليل.

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r2.speaker: أبو الليث
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r2.claim: Abu al-Layth says the brothers came after the afternoon prayer.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r2.anchor: وفي تفسير أبي الليث بعد العصر

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r3.speaker: الكواشي
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r3.claim: Al-Kawashi says they came in the evening to make their excuse seem more emphatic.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r3.anchor: قال في الكواشي : وإنما جاؤوا عشاء ليقدموا على المبالغة في الاعتذار.

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r4.claim: Their crying is circumstantial and means that they pretended to cry; Persian glosses it as deliberate weeping.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r4.anchor:
يبكون حال ، أي : متباكين.
والتباكي بالفارسية (كريستن يدا كردن)

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r5.speaker: شريح
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r5.claim: When al-Shaʿbi assumed a crying wife in a case was wronged, Shurayh replied that Joseph’s brothers cried while guilty; judges must follow the prescribed Sunna, not tears.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r5.anchor: قد جاء أخوة يوسف يبكون وهم ظلمة ولا ينبغي أن يقضي إلا بما أمر أن يقضي به

BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r6.claim: The Mathnawi says the brothers’ grief was a deception masking envy and malice.
BURSEVI:v4p145#3/r6.anchor:
كرهي اخوان يوسف حيلتست
كه درونشان رز رشك وعلتست

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r2.claim: Enabling a liar to weep at will is a sign of God’s abandonment.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r2.anchor: تمكين الكذاب من البكاء سمة خذلان الله تعالى إياه

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r3.claim: An unattributed report says that when hypocrisy is complete, a person can control his eyes and weep whenever he wishes.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r3.anchor: إذا كمل نفاق المرء ملك عينه حتى يبكي ما شاء

QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r4.claim: Qushayri allows that the brothers may have regretted harming Joseph and wept sincerely, while concealing the reason from Jacob and blaming the wolf.
QUSHAYRI:v2p70/r4.anchor: لا يبعد أن يقال إنهم وإن جنوا على يوسف عليه السلام فقد ندموا على ما فعلوا

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r1.claim: The brothers came to their father as lying sinners.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r1.anchor: سمعت أبا بكر بن عياش يذكر ، عن جراد الضبي قال : انتهيت إلى الحسن وهو يقص وهو يقول : اتو اباهم كذبة اثمة

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r2.claim: The brothers slaughtered a young sheep, smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt, and came to Jacob crying at night.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r2.anchor: عن السدي قال ثم انهم رجعوا إلى ابيهم فاخذوا جديا من الغنم فذبحوه ونضحوا دمه على القميص ثم اقبلوا على ابيهم عشاء يبكون

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r3.claim: After the caravan departed with Joseph and his brothers realized he was gone, they came crying to their father at night.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2110/r3.anchor: قال : قال محمد بن اسحاق : فلما انطلقت به العير ، وعرف اخوته ان قد ذهب به ، جاءوا اباهم عشاء يبكون .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r1.claim: One group reads ʿishāʾ, evening time; al-Hasan reads ʿashiyan, likened by Abu al-Fath to a plural form with a dropped tāʾ for ease, as in a line by ʿAdī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r1.anchor: قرأت فرقة «عشاء» أي وقت العشاء، وقرأ الحسن: «عشى» على مثال دجى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r2.claim: The author explains the wording as their eyes becoming blurred from crying, like the cloudy gaze of a weeping person; Shurayh compared a false woman’s weeping to theirs and recited the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r2.anchor: ومعنى ذلك أصابهم عشا من البكاء أو شبه العشا إذ كذلك هي هيئة عين الباكي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r3.claim: A report says Jacob first asked whether the sheep had suffered harm; when they said no, he asked where Joseph was, then wept, cried aloud, and asked for Joseph’s shirt.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p226/r3.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب لما سمع بكاءهم قال: ما بالكم أجرى في الغنم شيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r1.claim: Abu Hurayra, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Sumayfiʿ, and al-Aʿmash read ʿishāʾ with a ḍamma on the first letter.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r1.anchor: وقرأ أبو هريرة والحسن وابن السميفع والأعمش عشاء بضم العين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r2.claim: They came at nightfall because darkness made them bolder in presenting their fabricated excuse.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p191/r2.anchor: جاؤوا وقت العتمة ليكونوا أجرأ في الظلمة على الاعتذار بالكذب

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.claim: The common reading is ḏal with zāy in ‘lying blood’; ʿĀʾisha's reading uses dāl and means fresh blood.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r1.anchor: قراءة العامة: بدم كذب بالذال معجمة من فوق، وعن عائشة: بدم [كدب] بالدال

JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r6.claim: ʿAshāʾ may mean the day's end, first darkness, a broad period from noon to morning, or time from sunset prayer to night; with fatḥa it means food.
JISHUMI:v5p3610#2/r6.anchor: العشاء: آخر النهار، وهو طرف من أطراف الزمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r1.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ʿashiyyan as a diminutive; Ibn Jinnī reports a short form with ḍamma and says they were blinded by weeping.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r1.anchor: وعن الحسن ( عشيا ) على تصغير عشى يقال : لقيته عشيا وعشيانا ، وأصيلا وأصيلانا ورواه ابن جني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r2.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r2.claim: When a woman cried before Shurayḥ, al-Shaʿbī noted Joseph’s brothers also wept despite being wrongdoers; judgment follows the prescribed Sunnah.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r2.anchor: فقال له الشعبي : يا أبا أمية ، أما تراها تبكي ؟ فقال : قد جاء إخوة يوسف يبكون وهم ظلمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r3.claim: A report says Jacob panicked at their voices, asked whether the flock was harmed, then asked why they had come and where Joseph was.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p424#2/r3.anchor: وروي أنه لما سمع صوتهم فزع وقال : ما لكم يا بني ؟ هل أصابكم في غنمكم شيء ؟

MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.claim: Joseph’s brothers come to Jacob at the evening prayer, claiming they went hunting and left Joseph guarding their belongings; the wolf ate him, they say, and Jacob will not believe them even if truthful.
MUQATIL:12:16-18/r1.anchor: { وجآءوا أباهم } يعقوب { عشآء يبكون } [آية: 16] صلاة العتمة.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.claim: They come at night to conceal the truth and embolden themselves to make an excuse.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ وجاؤوا أباهم عشاء ﴾ للاستتار والتجسر على الاعتذار

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.speaker: الأعمش
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.claim: Al-Aʿmash says no one should believe a person who cries after Joseph's brothers.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r2.anchor: حال عن الأعمش لا تصدق باكية بعد إخوة يوسف

NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.claim: Hearing their cries, Jacob is alarmed and asks if something happened to their flock, then asks what happened and where Joseph is.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p181#2/r3.anchor: فلما سمع صوتهم فزع وقال مالكم با بنى هل أصابكم فى غنمكم شيء قالوا لا قال فما بالكم وأين يوسف

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r1.claim: After throwing Joseph in the well, the brothers returned to Jacob at night crying; when he asked whether their flock had suffered, they said no, and he asked what became of Joseph.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r1.anchor: لما طرحوا يوسف في الجب رجعوا إلى أبيهم وقت العشاء باكين

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r2.speaker: ابن جني
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r2.claim: Ibn Jinnī reads ʿashāʾ with a ḍamma on the first letter and a shortened ending, explaining it by eyes clouded from crying.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r2.anchor: ورواه ابن جني / عشا بضم العين والقصر وقال : عشوا من البكاء

RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r3.speaker: شريح
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r3.claim: In a court case, al-Shaʿbī asks why a woman is crying; judge Shurayḥ replies that Joseph's brothers also cried while being oppressive liars, so a judge must rule only by truth.
RAZI-FULL:v18p81/r3.anchor: وروي أن امرأة تحاكمت إلى شريح فبكت فقال الشعبي : يا أبا أمية ما تراها تبكي ؟ قال : قد جاء إخوة يوسف يبكون وهم ظلمة كذبة

SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r1.claim: عشاء is properly a time adverb, while يبكون is a circumstantial clause meaning they came weeping; the alternative reading as a plural noun is rejected.
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r1.anchor: أحدهما: وهو الذي لا ينبغي أن يقال غيره أنه ظرف زمان، أي: جاؤوه في هذا الوقت

SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r2.claim: He analyzes the ḍamma reading عشآء as a plural, with alternate morphological derivations such as عشاة losing its feminine ending.
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r2.anchor: ويقرأ بضم العين، والأصل: عشاة مثل غاز وغزاة، فحذفت الهاء وزيدت الألف

SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r3.speaker: الحسن البصري
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r3.claim: Hasan's عشآء reading derives from العشوة, darkness; he also reads عشا by removing the feminine ending and عشيا as a diminutive.
SAMIN-DURR:12:16/r3.anchor: قلت: وهذه القراءة قراءة الحسن البصري، وهي من العشوة والعشوة وهي الظلام

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r1.speaker: Bg, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r1.claim: Jacob became worried when his sons arrived weeping and asked whether anything had happened to their sheep in the pasture.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r1.anchor: Jacob became worried and asked them if anything had happened to their sheep that were out in the pasture (Bg, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r2.speaker: al-Qushayrī
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r2.claim: Their false tears show blatant hypocrisy; total hypocrites can control their eyes and cry at will.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r2.anchor: it was their hypocrisy that allowed them to lie in such a blatant manner, saying that when people become total hypocrites, they can control their eyes to the point that they can cry at will

STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.claim: Upon hearing Joseph was dead, Jacob fainted; the brothers poured water on him, and he remained unconscious until the next morning.
STUDYQURAN:12:16/r6.anchor: Jacob fainted, and the brothers poured water over him to wake him up. Yet he remained unconscious until early the next morning (Q)

TAB-FULL:v13p34/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r1.claim: Joseph’s brothers return to their father at night, crying after throwing Joseph into the well.
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r1.anchor: وجاء إخوة يوسف أباهم بعد ما ألقوا يوسف في غيابة الجب

TAB-FULL:v13p34/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r3.claim: Al-Suddi recounts Jacob asking what happened to the flock and Joseph, then demanding the shirt; the brothers bring it stained with blood, and Jacob weeps over it.
TAB-FULL:v13p34/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " أقبلوا على أبيهم عشاء يبكون فلما سمع أصواتهم فزع، وقال: ما لكم يا بني؟

ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p95/r3.claim: عشاء is an adverb of time.

TABATABAI:12:15-16/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:15-16/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:15-16/r8.claim: “Evening” means the end of the day, or the period from sunset prayer until night; the brothers wept to disguise their plot and win their father’s trust.
TABATABAI:12:15-16/r8.anchor: العشاء آخر النهار، وقيل من صلاة المغرب إلى العتمة، وإنما كانوا يبكون ليلبسوا الأمر على أبيهم

TABRISI:12:13-18/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r2.claim: Ḥuzn and aḥzan are both used for sorrow; shuʿūr is subtle perception, and ʿishāʾ may mean the late day, early night, or the period of the evening prayer.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r2.anchor: الشعور إدراك الشيء بمثل الشعرة في الدقة ومنه المشاعر في البدن

TABRISI:12:13-18/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r5.claim: The answer to “if the wolf eats him” is omitted after the oath: “when they took him away” means the plot they intended was grave. Kūfan grammarians treat the wāw in “and they agreed” as inserted, but Basrans reject that without proof and analyze the syntax otherwise.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r5.anchor: هي اللام التي يتلقى بها القسم { وإنا إذا لخاسرون } جواب القسم

TABRISI:12:13-18/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:13-18/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:13-18/r6.claim: Kūfans cite poetry for an inserted wāw in ajmaʿū; Basrans say the examples have an omitted answer, rejecting insertion as lacking evidence or analogy.
TABRISI:12:13-18/r6.anchor: والكوفيون يقولون: الواو في وأجمعوا مقحمة وتقديره أجمعوا

TABRISI:12:16-18/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:16-18/r1.claim: Jacob’s crying is parsed circumstantially, ʿishāʾ as a time adverb, and “we were racing” as another circumstantial clause; “while they did not realize” may modify either the later promise or the revelation.
TABRISI:12:16-18/r1.anchor: وقوله { يبكون } في موضع نصب على الحال وعشاء منصوب على الظرف

TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r3.claim: The brothers returned to Jacob at night or late afternoon to mislead him and make excuses more boldly; their tears were feigned to seem truthful, showing that crying does not prove a claim.
TABRISI:12:16-18#2/r3.anchor: أي ليلا أو في آخر النهار ليلبسوا على أبيهم وليكونوا أجرأ على الاعتذار

THALABI:v5p202/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p202/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p202/r1.claim: The brothers came at night weeping to make their false excuse easier to present; another explanation says they delayed until evening to deceive Jacob.
THALABI:v5p202/r1.anchor: وجاؤ أباهم عشاء يبكون ليكونوا أجرأ في الظلمة على الاعتذار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r1.claim: The brothers slaughtered a lamb, smeared its blood on Joseph’s shirt, and had left him naked in the well.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r1.anchor: ذبحوا سخلة وجلوا دمها على قميص يوسف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r2.claim: They came in the evening to use the darkness to excuse themselves and make their deception more persuasive; their weeping was staged to seem innocent of the alleged wolf attack.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r2.anchor: ليكونوا أجرا في الظلمة على الاعتذار وترويج

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r3.speaker: مجالد عن الشعبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r3.claim: Shurayḥ answered a woman who wept in court by recalling that Joseph’s brothers had also come to their father weeping at night.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p43#2/r3.anchor: قد جاء إخوة يوسف أباهم عشاء يبكون

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The brothers probably returned late at night to prevent Jacob from having a chance to search for Joseph.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The reason that the brothers came back late in the night probably was to rule out any chance of going in search of him

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.claim: Omitting a recoverable object can make speech more graceful; in وجد من دونهم امرأتين تذودان, the omitted object is their camels, and poetry likewise leaves objects understood.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r1.anchor: أي: تذودان إبلهما، ولو نطق بالمفعول لما كان في عذوبة حذفه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r2.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r2.claim: Dhu al-Rumma's description praises balanced speech: its edges neither spill into rambling nor become too spare for what listeners need.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r2.anchor: رخيم الحواشي؛ أي: لا تنتشر حواشيه فتهرأ فيه

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r3.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r3.claim: The line خير الحديث ما كان لحنا means speech may be deliberately oblique, not grammatically faulty; the Prophetic phrase ألحن بحجته means more adept at arguing a case.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r3.anchor: وليس من اللحن الذي هو إفساد الإعراب، ذلك حديث غير هذا

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r4.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r4.claim: Via Isa ibn Maymun, al-Hasan reads عشا as people blinded by weeping, deriving it from عَشاة with its feminine ending omitted; Abu al-Fath calls this weak because one day's crying would not blind them.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p333/r4.anchor: ما رواه عيسى بن ميمون عن الحسن أنه قرأ: "وجاءوا أباهم عشا يبكون"

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r1.claim: A narrative says the brothers had Joseph ask to go, Jacob promised permission the next morning, then farewell blessings and an embrace; they carried him while visible, then threw him down when out of sight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r1.anchor: حكي أنهم قالوا ليوسف: اطلب من أبيك أن يبعثك معنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r2.claim: Commentators transmit many detailed tales about Joseph being cast into the well and pleading with his brothers, but neither Qur'an nor sound hadith establishes them; Abu Hayyan says to consult tafsir books without treating them as established.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r2.anchor: وذكر المفسرون أشياء كثيرة تتضمن كيفية إلقائه في غيابة الجب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r3.claim: The passage omits a connective clause recoverable from context: Jacob granted the request and sent Joseph with them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r3.anchor: وبين هذه الجملة والجمل التي قبلها محذوف يدل عليه المعنى تقديره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r5.claim: Grammarians disagree whether the answer to 'when' is explicit: some take the brothers' later speech or 'We inspired him,' allowing an extra conjunction per Kufan usage; Basrans posit an omitted answer, for which several estimates are offered.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p247/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في جواب لما أهو مثبت؟ أم محذوف؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r6.claim: 'At evening' is an adverb or derives from darkness; Hasan's forms may be a plural of evening or a diminutive, with a reading reflecting deletion of feminine tā'.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r6.anchor: وعشاء نصب على الظرف، أو من العشوة. والعشوة: الظلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r7.claim: One explanation says the brothers came at night because darkness made their excuse easier; a proverb advises against seeking favors at night or apologizing for sin in daylight.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p248/r7.anchor: قيل: وإنما جاؤوا عشاء ليكون أقدر على الاعتذار في الظلمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r1.claim: The passage omits that the brothers arrived without Joseph; Jacob asked where he was and they answered that a wolf ate him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r1.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره: وجاؤوا أباهم دون يوسف عشاء يبكون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r2.claim: A report has Jacob ask whether something happened to the flock; after their answer he collapses, and Judah checks for signs of life and laments that they have lost their brother and killed their father with grief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r2.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب لما سمع بكاءهم قال: ما لكم، أجرى في الغنم شيء؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r3.speaker: الأعمش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r3.claim: Al-A'mash says no weeping person should be believed after Joseph's brothers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p249/r3.anchor: قال الأعمش: لا يصدق باك بعد إخوة يوسف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r1.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r1.claim: ʿAshāʾ is the interval from sunset prayer until night prayer; العشاآن names the two evening prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r1.anchor: كما قال الراغب من صلاة المغرب إلى العتمة والعشاآن : المغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan is said to have read عَشِيًّا as a diminutive; another reading عَشِيّ has a shortened form and is variously analyzed as a plural or as an original form altered by sound change.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه قرأ عشيا بضم العين وفتح الشين وتشديد الياء منونا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r3.claim: The alternative construals of the nonstandard readings face objections: the proposed حذف of tāʾ and plural pattern are not licensed, so another vocalic-shift and elision account is offered.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r3.anchor: وأورد عليهما بأنه لا جواز لمثل هذا الحذف وأنه لا يجمع أفعل فعلاء

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r4.claim: A proposed reading takes the word as a plural of عشوة, a venture in darkness or confusion, emphasizing the brothers' deceit; another takes it as a flame, emphasizing their haste and glee.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : هو جمع عشوة مثلث العين وهي ركوب أمر على غير بصيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r5.claim: The ordinary reading means evening; they may have returned then because they could not reach home sooner or because darkness made their excuse easier to stage.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r5.anchor: والظاهر الأول وإنما جاءوا عشاء إما لأنها لا يصلوا من مكانهم إلا في ذلك الوقت

ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r6.claim: Some take this as the evening of the same day, while others infer a later evening from a report that Joseph stayed in the well three days and Judah brought him food.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p198#2/r6.anchor: ظاهر كلان بعضهم الأول وذهب بعضهم إلى الثاني بناءا على ما روي

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r1.claim: Their weeping was feigned: they displayed tears without genuine grief, as liars commonly imitate sorrow.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r1.anchor: أي متباكين أي مظهرين البكاء بتكلف لأنه لم يكن عن حزن

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r2.speaker: الشعبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts a woman crying before the judge Shurayḥ; when people pointed to her tears, Shurayḥ recalled that Joseph's brothers came to their father crying.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r2.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن الشعبي قال : جاءت إمرأة إلى شريح تخاصم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r3.speaker: الأعمش
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r3.claim: Al-Aʿmash quips that after Joseph's brothers, even one's father should not be believed.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r3.anchor: وقال الأعمش : لا يصدق أباك بعد إخوة يوسف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r4.claim: In a report, Jacob asks whether some wage has afflicted them; when they say no, he asks what happened to them and where Joseph is.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p199/r4.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما سمع بكاءهم قال : ما بالكم أجري

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r1.claim: Some rhetoricians say the brothers arrived at nightfall to make their fabricated excuse easier to deliver in darkness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r1.anchor: {وجاءوا أباهم عشاء يبكون} قال أهل المعاني: جاؤوا في ظلمة العشاء ليكونوا أجرأ على الاعتذار بالكذب.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r2.claim: A report says Jacob heard their cries and wailing, came out, asked if something had happened to their flock, and when they said no, asked what had happened and where Joseph was.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p222/r2.anchor: وروي أن يعقوب عليه السلام سمع صياحهم وعويلهم فخرج وقال: ما لكم يا بني هل أصابكم في غنمكم شيء؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r1.claim: ʿAshāʾ means late day; readings include its diminutive ʿashiyyan and ʿashiyan as a plural for people made blind by crying.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r1.anchor: عشاء } أي آخر النهار. وقرىء «عشيا» وهو تصغير عشي وعشي بالضم والقصر جمع أعشى

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r2.claim: Their crying is affected rather than genuine; a report says Jacob heard it, became alarmed, and asked what was wrong and where Joseph was.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:16/r2.anchor: يبكون } متباكين. روي أنه لما سمع بكاءهم فزع وقال ما لكم يا بني وأين يوسف.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r1.claim: The brothers came at night so Jacob would not read their faces in daylight; a saying likewise counsels seeking favors by night and avoiding daytime apologies.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r1.anchor: في ظلمة الليل لئلا يتفرس أبيهم في وجوههم إذا رآها

BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r2.claim: Their tears do not establish truth, since crying can be feigned; crying is the flow of tears from the eye in sadness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p16/r2.anchor: والآية دالة على أن البكاء لا يدل على الصدق

ALUSI-FULL:v13p74#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p74#2/r12.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p74#2/r12.claim: One view says the brothers’ evening tears were performed: they achieved their aim and disguised joy as grief in darkness; daylight would expose them.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p74#2/r12.anchor: قيل : إن ذلك كان بكاء فرح بظفرهم بمقصودهم لكنهم أظهروا أنه بكاء حزن

ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r1.claim: A couplet says one distinguishes genuine weeping from imitation when tears cross the cheek.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p75/r1.anchor: إذا اشتبكت دموع في خدود تبين من بكى ممن تباكى

NAHHAS:v2p317/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p317/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p317/r5.claim: يبكون is a circumstantial clause describing the brothers' state.
NAHHAS:v2p317/r5.anchor: في موضع الحال قال محمد بن يزيد

TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.speaker: علي بن الحسين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.claim: In Abu Hamza's report, Jacob's sons planned to kill Yusuf, but their eldest persuaded them to cast him into a well; they later lied that a wolf ate him, and Jacob grieved yet trusted the truthful dream God had shown him.
TABATABAI:12:21#4/r1.anchor: فقال كبيرهم { لا تقتلوا يوسف } ولكن { ألقوه في غيابت الجب يلتقطه بعض السيارة إن كنتم فاعلين }

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r2.claim: The blood on Joseph's shirt was fabricated and was not his blood.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p318#3/r2.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وجاؤوا على قميصه بدم كذب ﴾ قال كان ذلك الدم كذبا لم يكن دم يوسف

BURHAN:v4p107/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.claim: Sometimes an apparent sequence is a resumption with an omitted question: after the brothers arrive crying, an imagined “what did they say?” is answered by “O our father,” so there is no conjunction.
BURHAN:v4p107/r1.anchor: الحال الرابعة إن يكون بتقدير الاستئناف كأن قائلا قال لم كان كذا فقيل كذا فهاهنا لا عطف أيضا

BURHAN:v4p66/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p66/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p66/r3.claim: A present verb in a circumstantial phrase depicts action underway at the time of arrival and renewing moment by moment, as in ‘they came to their father weeping.’
BURHAN:v4p66/r3.anchor: إذ المراد إن يريد صورة ما هم عليه وقت المجئ وأنهم آخذون في البكاء يجددونه شيئا بعد شئ

ITQAN:v2p578#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r3.claim: An imperfect form after a past event portrays the state at that moment and its ongoing renewal, a device called narration of a past scene as present.
ITQAN:v2p578#2/r3.anchor: إذ المراد أن يفيد صورة ما هم عليه وقت المجيء وأنهم آخذون في البكاء يجددونه شيأ بعد شيء وهو المسمي حكاية الحال الماضية
